Heard Sri. Prashant Mathapati, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Praveena Y Devareddiyavara, learned HCGP for the respondent-State.
2. The petitioner/accused is seeking regular bail in Crime No.18/2024 of Kundagol Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B, 34 of IPC 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act of 1961.

Brief facts of the case:
3. It is the case of the prosecution that the complainant being father of the deceased has lodged a complaint stating that he performed the marriage of his daughter who is deceased in this case.
As per the averments of the complaint and statement of the complainant, his daughter was staying with her in-laws and husband in her matrimonial home after the marriage.

The petitioner herein being accused No.1 was not taking proper care of his wife and used to come to his house in NC:
2024:KHC-D:7567 the late hours.

Whenever the deceased asked about the said late coming, he was abusing and assaulting her.
4.
The relationship between the petitioner herein and the deceased was not cordial.
The deceased had informed the complainant about the said fact.
It is further stated in this complaint that all the accused were demanding additional dowry in the form of cash and gold and used to harass the deceased both mentally and physically.
Consequently, his daughter stated to have committed suicide on 06.02.2024 around 8.30 a.m., in her matrimonial house.
The complainant lodged a complaint against the in-laws and husband of the deceased.
The jurisdictional police after conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
The petitioner being accused No.1 has been denied bail by the Trial Court.
Hence, the petitioner approached this Court seeking regular bail.

5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the ingredients of Section 304-B of IPC cannot be attracted and one of the ingredients, namely, NC: 2024:KHC-D:7567 "Soon before death" is absent.
To attract the provision, she must have been subjected to cruelty and harassment before her death.
The same is absent in the complaint as well as in the statement of the complainant.
6. It is further submitted that the complainant has given two versions.
In one version of his statement, he included the brother of the petitioner, however, in another statement, he withdrew the inclusion of the brother of the petitioner.

7. It is further submitted that the petitioner and others have not committed any offence as stated by the complainant.
The petitioner is the resident of Chakalabbi village, Kundagol Taluk.
He will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.

8. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submits that petitioner No.1 being the husband, he was not cordial NC: 2024:KHC-D:7567 with the deceased, as per the averments of the complaint.
The complainant in his statement made before the Magistrate has categorically stated that the petitioner used to harass the deceased in one or the other pretext and he was not in good terms with her.
The petitioner along with his family members were demanding dowry in the form of cash and gold and used to torture her.
Consequently, she committed suicide in her matrimonial home.

Since there is a presumption available to the victim,
the burden heavily lies to the petitioner and others to rebut the presumption.
Therefore, they are not entitled for bail.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail and bail application has to be rejected.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the complaint and further statement of the complainant, it appears that he made omnibus allegations against the petitioner and other accused in respect of demand of dowry.
In addition to the said demand of dowry, further, NC: 2024:KHC-D:7567 the complainant states in his complaint that the petitioner was not in cordial terms with the deceased.

However, even after four years of her marriage, neither any panchayat held nor any complaint had been filed before the competent authority and moreover, the ingredients of the provision under Section 304-B of IPC prima facie is not made out.
Therefore, it is appropriate to grant him bail by imposing suitable conditions.

10. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No. 18/2024 of Kundagol Police Station, on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7567 a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
